to approximately 1450 B.C.E., in which year Joshua probably died
At the age of 110 years, Joshua died and was buried at Timnath-serah.

events.notes: The 1971 Aid book suggested Joshua's death 'may have occurred within twenty or thirty years after the conquest'; current publications give c. 1450.

events.description_en: Joshua wrote the book bearing his name in Canaan; it covers over 20 years from the entry into Canaan in 1473 to about 1450 B.C.E.

events.description_en: Caleb, who with Joshua had given a faithful report as a spy, died about this time.

sources.quote_en: Caleb dies (age c. 102)

events.description_en: After Joshua's death, Jehovah raised up judges to deliver Israel from oppressors; the book of Judges covers roughly 330 years down to the time of Samuel. Some judgeships evidently overlapped.

sources.quote_en: Naomi, Ruth, Deborah, Barak, Jael, Gideon, Samson, Jephthah and his daughter 1450*-1120* B.C.E.
Time Covered: c. 1450–c. 1120 B.C.E.
covers a period of some 330 years between Israel’s conquest of Canaan and the beginning of the monarchy
So the period of the Judges extended about 300 years.
these 356 years (from Israel’s entry into Canaan in 1473 B.C.E. until the start of Saul’s reign in 1117 B.C.E.)
beginning of time period of judges and saviors of Israel

conflicts.note: Insight 'Judge' says the period of the Judges (Othniel to Samuel) extended about 300 years; Insight 'Judges, Book of' says the book covers some 330 years.

events.title_en: Eli serves as high priest and judges Israel 40 years
events.description_en: Eli, a descendant of Aaron through Ithamar, served as high priest and judged Israel for 40 years; Samuel began to be a prophet during his lifetime.

sources.quote_en: As high priest, Eli judged Israel for 40 years.
Eli’s priesthood must have begun more than 60 years prior to Saul’s reign

events.notes: Year field 1177 is derived from the Aid book's statement 'more than 60 years prior to Saul's reign' (1117 B.C.E.); no publication prints 1177.

events.title_en: Jephthah defeats Ammon and begins six-year judgeship
events.description_en: Jephthah of Gilead defeated the Ammonites, fulfilled his vow regarding his daughter, and judged Israel six years. His reference to '300 years' of Israelite control east of the Jordan helps place his judgeship.

sources.quote_en: Jephthah’s reference to “three hundred years” of Israelite control E of the Jordan would seem to place the start of his six-year judgeship around 1173 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Ark captured by the Philistines; Eli dies
events.description_en: Israel was defeated by the Philistines, Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas died, and the Ark was captured; on hearing the news, 98-year-old Eli fell and died.

sources.quote_en: Blind and feeble, 98-year-old Eli ... Upon hearing that the Ark has been captured, Eli falls over backward and dies
the ark of the covenant was in Kiriath-jearim for 20 years subsequent to his death and up to the Israelite victory over Philistia, which preceded Saul’s reign

events.notes: No year is printed. Aid places Eli's death more than 20 years before Saul's reign (1117 B.C.E.); sort_key is an ordering placeholder only.

events.title_en: Ark returned; kept at Kiriath-jearim 20 years
events.description_en: After God struck the Philistines with plagues, they returned the Ark; it was brought to Kiriath-jearim, where it remained 20 years until after Israel turned back to Jehovah.

sources.title_en: What Is the Ark of the Covenant?
sources.quote_en: God struck them with plagues until they returned it to Israel.
Ark of covenant in Kiriath-jearim 20 years

events.notes: No year printed; ordering placeholder.

events.title_en: Samuel judges Israel; victory over the Philistines at Mizpah (Ebenezer)
events.description_en: Over 20 years after the Ark's capture, Israel abandoned idols at Samuel's urging; when the Philistines attacked at Mizpah, Jehovah threw them into confusion, and Samuel set up the stone Ebenezer. Samuel went on judging Israel.

sources.quote_en: Jehovah answered Samuel’s prayer, throwing the Philistines into confusion and thereby enabling the Israelites to gain a decisive victory.
Samuel leads Israel to victory over Philistia (1 Samuel 7:7-14) ... 1117 B.C.E.

events.notes: Aid chart places this victory shortly before Saul's reign began in 1117 B.C.E., with an indeterminate intervening period.

events.description_en: Samuel evidently wrote Judges in Israel after Saul became king (1117) and before David captured Zion (1070); it covers c. 1450–c. 1120 B.C.E.

sources.quote_en: It must therefore be dated between 1117 and 1070 B.C.E.
